title: Empty --stats-out path token silently disables telemetry in both binaries, defeating the W1 fix contract
evidence:
app/main.odin:144-151:
	stats_path := ""
	for i := 1; i < len(os.args); i += 1 {
		if os.args[i] == "--stats-out" {
			if i+1 >= len(os.args) || stats_path != "" {
				fmt.eprintln("usage: app [--stats-out <path>]")
				os.exit(2)
			}
			stats_path = os.args[i+1]
app/main.odin:176:
	app.stats_live = stats_path != ""
harness/main.odin:121:
			stats_out = rest[i+1]
harness/main.odin:128:
	if stats_out != "" && len(filtered) != 1 {
harness/run.odin:295:
	stats_live := stats_out != ""
detail: `--stats-out ""` (e.g. an unset shell variable) passes every check in both parsers; stats_live becomes false and the run exits 0 with telemetry silently off — the exact state the W1 fix comment forbids ("never silently run telemetry-off").
recommended_fix: Reject an empty path token in both parsers: after `stats_path = os.args[i+1]` / `stats_out = rest[i+1]`, treat an empty (or flag-shaped) token as a usage error with exit 2.

title: Harness accepts a flag-shaped --stats-out path token and writes a stray file; the app rejects the same argv with exit 2
detail: `harness run demo --stats-out --stats-out` sets stats_out to the literal "--stats-out" (i += 2 consumes it as the path) and writes a stray file named `--stats-out` in cwd; the app rejects the identical argv shape with exit 2. Divergent validation at the shared flag boundary.
recommended_fix: Validate the path token in the harness parse — reject a token equal to "--stats-out" or starting with "-" (usage/exit 2), mirroring the app's stricter behavior.

title: CI's new PP_DEBUG build writes app-debug.bin, which the .gitignore binary rule (app.bin only) does not cover
evidence:
.github/workflows/ci.yml:105-106:
      - name: PP_DEBUG overlay build (compile gate)
        run: odin build app -define:PP_DEBUG=true -out:app-debug.bin
.gitignore:24-25:
# local build output — never commit binaries
app.bin
(git check-ignore app-debug.bin → no match; app.bin → .gitignore:25)
detail: The new gate invites developers to replicate the build locally; the resulting binary embeds the §7.6 debug/cheat tooling yet evades the repo's never-commit-binaries ignore rule — an accidentally-committed debug build ships the tooling the compile gate exists to exclude.
recommended_fix: Extend the ignore rule to cover the debug artifact (e.g. `app-debug.bin` or `app*.bin`) next to the existing `app.bin` entry.
